key_insight: FLORE aims to teach humanoids to coordinate contact forces with hand and whole-body motion, rather than relying on motion trajectories alone. It uses human demonstrations recorded without a robot.
problem_solved: Everyday physical tasks require controlling both movement and contact force across two hands and the body—requirements that kinematic trajectories alone cannot capture.
method: Introduce FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid locomotion and manipulation.
Collect hand motion and contact forces and torques using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers.
Record body motion with wearable trackers to capture coordinated hand–body demonstrations.
impact: For robotics practitioners, FLORE highlights a way to collect demonstrations that capture physical interaction as well as movement. The provided abstract is truncated, so its training details and evaluation results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Human demonstrator with two force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers.
Data-flow diagram: hand motion + contact forces and torques + body motion → FLORE → humanoid control.
Humanoid silhouette with force arrows at both hands and motion arrows across the body.
Side-by-side conceptual comparison of trajectory-only control and force-aware whole-body coordination.
paper_authors: Sihang Li, Xiaofeng Guo, Jinkun Cao, Charlie Cheng, Ruihan Yang
